question: Does detcore's sysinfo(2) handler write uninitialized padding into guest memory, and which sibling handlers share the pattern?

hermit.before_binary: hermit 0.2.0 (gf89c69766371), clean-tree debug build at hermit main tip f89c69766371806d3c9b2c3003531df2d59d6118
hermit.after_binary: built in worktrees/det2/hermit at detached f89c69766371 with a LOCAL-ONLY [patch] redirecting the pinned Reverie git source to worktrees/det2/reverie; the patch was reverted after the build and neither hermit file was committed

assurance: L0 for the Reverie change (reverie workspace suite green). The before/after guest measurements are single-run observations under --strict, not an L2 claim.

host.libunwind: /home/newton/fbsource/fbcode/third-party-buck/platform010/build/libunwind (not installed system-wide; PKG_CONFIG_PATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH required to build and run)

limitations: The black-box audit covers 23 struct-writing syscalls; absence of a flag is weaker evidence than presence, because a leak is only visible when the residue happens to differ between the paired calls. It is complemented by a source-level classification of all 70 write_value/write_values sites in hermit.

Four probes (getrusage_self, clock_gettime, gettimeofday, adjtimex) are indeterminate natively as well -- they carry genuinely time-varying fields -- so the discriminator cannot rule on them. waitid is likewise not discriminable: the raw syscall leaves most of siginfo_t untouched on native Linux.
x86_64 only. The padding windows (82..88, 108..112) are x86_64 layout; aarch64 was not measured.
The Reverie fix is not pushed and has no PR: egress to github.com returns proxy 403 and the task was scoped local, no egress.
